evidence.observation: The plan says: '**GO2-C1** a proposal of four operations, one of which the candidate validation refuses: the preview names all four, three `admitted` and one refused with its verdict, exit 3' and 'A refusal that names no element stays a refusal of the whole proposal and the preview says so in one row.' All of them are built from the loaded candidate (_validated_candidate, service.py:1507-1518). A candidate that fails validation raises EvolutionError inside _load_model_document (service.py:294-295), and no preview exists. policy_issues work today only because the candidate has already validated by then (service.py:1534-1537).

concerns.recommendation: Add a decision on what document carries the outcomes of a refused proposal. Either use a refusal report separate from EvolutionPreview, or make the candidate-derived preview fields optional. Say what apply does with that document, and add a criterion that apply refuses it.
concerns.title: GO2-C1 needs a preview of a candidate that fails validation, and the preview model cannot hold one

evidence.observation: The plan says: '**GO2-C3** a proposal admitted today has every operation `admitted` and every other preview field byte-identical, apart from the schema version', 'The preview's schema version moves', D2 '(a) A new `operation_outcomes` list in the preview, under a new preview schema version', and R0.3 'a proposal admitted today has every other field unchanged'. In the code, _bindings_match refuses a preview whose version differs from its proposal's ('preview and proposal versions must match', evolve/models.py:1096-1097), and preview() refuses any proposal that is not at EVOLUTION_SCHEMA_VERSION (service.py:1557-1561). Moving the preview version therefore moves the proposal version, and every v3 proposal a host holds is refused. proposal_sha256 is canonical_sha256 over the proposal (models.py:720-721), and preview_sha256 binds the whole body (models.py:1160-1162), so both digests change and GO2-C3 fails. Precedent at models.py:867-875: optional fields omitted when unset kept the bytes and preview_sha256 with no version move.

concerns.recommendation: Either add operation_outcomes under the _OPTIONAL_PREVIEW_FIELDS omit-when-unset rule without moving the version, or decouple the preview version from the proposal version in a stated decision. Restate GO2-C3 to exclude the digests that must change, and record in §5 the cost of the version move for v3 proposals.
concerns.title: GO2-C3 cannot hold: moving the preview schema version moves the proposal version and changes every digest

evidence.observation: The plan says: '**GO5-C2** a round that proposes nothing and a round whose proposals all map onto existing elements give different summaries' and 'GND computes the summary from the proposal and its preview ... The host supplies what it dropped before the proposal as an input file'. In the code, EvolutionProposal.operations is Field(min_length=1) (evolve/models.py:647-651), so a round that proposes nothing has no proposal or preview to summarize. A reply that only reuses existing ids and adds no rows (the GO4 rule) produces no operation either. D4(a)'s input file lists drops, not reuses, and the shape report (H18) covers only added fact types. No input named in the plan tells the two rounds apart, and telling them apart is the point of #227.

concerns.recommendation: Define the source of 'mapped onto existing elements', for example by having the host file also list reused ids, or by having the summary read the reply. Define the summary for a round with no proposal. Build GO5-C2's two fixtures so they differ only in that input.
concerns.title: GO5-C2 cannot be met: an empty round has no proposal, and reused elements leave no operation

evidence.observation: D1 proposes '(a) ... each tied to its operation where the refusal names an element' and '(a). A refusal that names no element stays a whole-proposal refusal and says so'. GO2-C2 says '**GO2-C2** one case per verdict word, each reachable with a committed fixture', and the verdict list includes `refused-by-d12`. In the code, every refusal in _enforce_d12 (service.py:428-477) names no element, for example 'new induced constraints must be proposed/deontic (D-12)', and the loop raises at the first failing constraint. _model_warnings also raises on layer-1 issues before layer 2 runs (model/__init__.py:302-304). Under D1(a), then, `refused-by-d12` can never be a per-operation verdict. An operation marked `admitted` after one pass may also hide a refusal that the first one masked, so GO3-C1 holds only for fixtures with a single fault.

concerns.recommendation: State in GO2 that the D-12 gate and candidate validation will collect every refusal with its host or locator, keeping today's first message and exit for the whole-proposal path. Otherwise, define `admitted` as 'no refusal found in this pass' and have the narrowed proposal re-previewed. Add a fixture with two faults in two different operations.
concerns.title: Under D1(a) no D-12 refusal can be tied to an operation, and a single pass cannot establish `admitted`

evidence.observation: The plan says: '**GO3-C3** ... applying the original preview after narrowing is refused as any stale preview is', and §6 says 'and the original preview stale'. GO3 is a library function that returns a new proposal and writes nothing (§2, D5 a). Apply refuses a preview as stale only when the live model's sha differs from preview.before_model.sha256 (service.py:2187-2191; 'stale' maps to exit 11, cli_service.py:283-334). After narrowing alone the model has not changed. If apply refuses the original preview, it does so by re-running validation and policy (service.py:2142-2153, :2203-2210), and that refusal has a different message and exit.

concerns.recommendation: Split GO3-C3 into two cases. First, before the narrowed proposal is applied, apply refuses the original preview through revalidation, with today's message and exit. Second, after the narrowed proposal is applied, apply refuses the original preview as a stale model CAS, exit 11.
concerns.title: GO3-C3 expects the original preview to go stale, but narrowing changes no model bytes

evidence.location: §2 GO1; §1 H5; GO1 spec lines 114-117 and T5 line 170
evidence.observation: The plan says the parse returns 'the document it already built for the same bytes and the same reader', and H5 says 'reads `source` only for its suffix (`.json` selects the strict JSON reader) ... For the same bytes and the same reader it returns equal documents'. Spec lines 114-117 define the reader as 'the value of the parser's own reader test ... (`_parsing.py:37`: the `.json` suffix, or text that starts with `{`)'. But _parsing.py:46-50 refuse a JSONDecodeError only under a .json suffix and otherwise fall back to YAML. Bytes like '{version: 5, ...}' are refused under model.orm.json, parse under model.orm.yaml, and share that key. In apply, _parse_model_text parses the current text under 'model.orm.yaml' (service.py:344, called at :2145) before _load_model_document reads the same bytes under the workspace name (:2203). With a .json workspace and a hand-built preview, the cached YAML document would be returned, and today's 'model JSON input refused' would disappear, against R0.2 and R0.3. Spec T5 catches this only if its bytes do not start with '{'.

concerns.recommendation: Key the cache on (sha256, Path(source).suffix == '.json'); that is the only way source changes a successful parse. Make T5 use YAML-flow bytes that start with '{' under both names, and expect the .json refusal even after the .yaml parse succeeded.
concerns.title: GO1's cache key treats the strict JSON reader and the JSON-then-YAML fallback as one reader

evidence.location: §3 table GO4 and GO5 rows; §3 Order; H21
evidence.observation: The GO5 row needs only 'GO2 merged into the branch; D4 ruled', yet it changes '`unattended-growth.md`'. The GO4 row needs 'VG2 and VG5 of reviewed-vocabulary-growth merged or not started (H21)'. Order: 'GO4 at any point after its ruling'. H21: 'VG1, then GO1, then VG2–VG5, then GO2–GO5'. GO2's start condition covers only VG2 and VG4, so GO5 can start while VG5 still has unattended-growth.md open. That is the two-writer case §6 claims to control. The 'or not started' clauses and 'any point' also let GO2 or GO4 land ahead of VG2–VG5, contrary to H21.

concerns.recommendation: Give GO5 the 'VG2 and VG5 merged' condition that GO4 has. Either drop 'or not started' and 'any point', or state that they amend the order H21 cites from the roadmap.
concerns.title: GO5 edits unattended-growth.md without the VG5 start condition, and GO4's timing contradicts H21's order

evidence.location: §4 GO1 row; §9 GO1 lane; Provenance lines 22-26
evidence.observation: The plan says: '**Which gate is which:** C1 to C4 read no clock and are the required regression gates; C5 compares two runs on one machine'. Yet the §9 GO1 lane runs `tests/test_go1_evolve_parse_once.py` and expects exit 0. The Provenance paragraph says: 'by up to 77 % for the sub-second and one-second timings at 604'. GO1 spec lines 155 and 173 put T8 (the C5 ratio) in that same file in the 'default lane'. T8 makes four apply runs at 604 object types, about 18 s by H6's figures. A scoped apply there takes about 2 s, inside the 77 % band, so a loaded runner can fail a lane the plan calls clock-free.

response.summary: GO1 holds up against the code. Every cited line in src/gnd matches this checkout, and the 22 and 6 parse counts agree with the call sites. No caller in evolve/service.py, model/__init__.py or model/_includes.py writes into the parsed document: compose and _merge clone, json_document rebuilds, and _finish_model takes shallow copies. R0.2 holds. GO1's one real defect is that its cache key treats the strict JSON reader and the JSON-then-YAML fallback as the same reader. GO2, GO3 and GO5 cannot be built or tested as written. GO2-C1 needs a preview of an invalid candidate, which the preview model cannot hold. GO2-C3 cannot hold once the schema version moves. Under D1(a), no D-12 refusal can be tied to an operation. GO3-C3 expects a stale preview that narrowing never creates. GO5-C2 has nothing to tell an empty round from a covered one. The one-writer order also leaves a gap: GO5 can edit unattended-growth.md while VG5 still has it open.

evidence.observation: The plan says the cache reuses a document for 'the same bytes and the same reader' and points to the GO1 draft spec. That spec (§6, lines 111–117) defines the reader key from '.json suffix, or text that starts with {'. In src/gnd/model/_parsing.py, a .yaml flow mapping such as {unquoted: value} falls back from JSON to YAML, while the same bytes named .json are refused. After the .yaml parse is cached, the proposed Boolean key would return its document for the .json call.

concerns.recommendation: Key the cache by the source mode that preserves strict .json refusal, and test YAML-first then JSON with the same YAML-only flow mapping.
concerns.title: GO1 cache can bypass strict JSON parsing

evidence.observation: GO2-C3 requires 'every other preview field byte-identical, apart from the schema version' after adding operation_outcomes. src/gnd/evolve/models.py:1160–1162 binds preview_sha256 to the serialized preview body, so that digest must change when the new field is added. Its validator also requires preview and embedded proposal versions to match; moving only the preview schema version is invalid.

concerns.recommendation: State the necessary digest and version changes explicitly, and limit byte-identity assertions to fields that can remain unchanged.
concerns.title: GO2 byte-identity criterion contradicts preview bindings

evidence.observation: The contract says 'GND computes the summary from the proposal and its preview', while GO5-C2 requires 'a round that proposes nothing'. Every EvolutionProposal wire version in src/gnd/evolve/models.py requires at least one operation, so an empty round has no proposal or preview to pass to the stated summary function.

concerns.recommendation: Define a summary input and output for a round with no proposal or preview, then use it in GO5-C2.
concerns.title: GO5 cannot summarize an empty round through its stated inputs

evidence.observation: The plan promises 'one row per operation' but says a refusal naming no element 'stays a refusal of the whole proposal and the preview says so in one row'. For a multi-operation proposal, the listed verdicts contain no status for operations whose admission was never assessed after that whole-proposal refusal. Today src/gnd/evolve/service.py raises EvolutionError before it constructs a preview in such cases.

concerns.recommendation: Specify a separate proposal-level refusal and an explicit unassessed operation status, or narrow the every-operation claim to previews that can assess every operation.

evidence.observation: GO3 is 'a library function' that returns a new proposal, but GO3-C3 says 'applying the original preview after narrowing is refused as any stale preview is'. Narrowing alone does not change the live model or the original preview's committed bytes; the current apply stale check in src/gnd/evolve/service.py:2188–2197 refuses it only after the live model changes.

evidence.observation: C2 includes 'a YAML model with a value JSON cannot spell', while C3 compares remembered documents. The GO1 draft spec §8 T3, line 168, makes that comparison with 'canonical JSON' for every T2 case. An unquoted YAML date is a supported non-JSON value in src/gnd/model/_documents.py, so canonical JSON cannot serialize that remembered document.

evidence.observation: GO1-C5 sets a pass threshold of 'at most 0.6' from runs 'in one test on one machine'. The plan itself records unchanged timings differing by up to 77% at the relevant size (lines 22–26). A same-machine ratio remains sensitive to load and run order.

evidence.location: R0.5, section 0, lines 71-74; risk table row 1, lines 257-258
evidence.observation: R0.5 writes: 'Anything GO1 remembers is keyed by the sha256 of the bytes it was computed from and is dropped when the command returns.' The §6 risk control repeats: 'the key is the sha256 of the bytes each caller already holds'. But src/gnd/model/_parsing.py:37 selects the strict JSON reader when 'Path(source).suffix == ".json" or text.lstrip().startswith("{")', and lines 46-49 refuse '{...'-prefixed bytes that are not valid JSON only when the source suffix is .json, falling through to the YAML reader otherwise — so identical bytes under different source names can legitimately parse differently or refuse differently (a .json-named load of '{a: 1}' raises ModelLoadError; the same bytes under a .yaml name load fine). §2 GO1 (lines 145-148) correctly states the cache returns the document 'for the same bytes and the same reader', and the GO1 draft spec's H5 row says the key accounts for the reader, so an implementer following §2 is safe.

concerns.recommendation: Amend R0.5 and the §6 risk row to state the key as (sha256 of bytes, reader identity) — the reader the source name selects — so the binding rule matches §2 and the spec; a bytes-only key would change refusals for '{...'-but-non-JSON bytes in a .json workspace model, which GO1-C2's '.json model' case would catch only after the fact.

Every code citation read was accurate: _load_model_document's three parses (service.py:264/277/291), the 22/6 parse counts' caller sites (:1507-1518, :1594, :2145, :2203, :2344, :2532, :2539), _parsing.py:25-56, input_policy.py guard_yaml, models.py schema versions and PolicyIssue, discover/output.py candidate_document/candidate_text, shapes.py, model_index.py index_scope, unattended-growth.md lines 235/286/57-73, and all nine §9 lane test files exist. response.summary: Plan r2 read in full and its citations verified at this checkout: H3-H5, H8-H12, H14, H16, H18, H21 and H22 all match (evolve/service.py, evolve/models.py, evolve/cli_service.py, model/_includes.py, model/__init__.py, model/_parsing.py, model_index.py, input_policy.py, discover/output.py, evolve/shapes.py, unattended-growth.md, the reviewed-vocabulary-growth plan and PROJECT.md, whose Proposed order gives VG1, GO1, VG2-VG5, GO2-GO5 exactly as H21 claims). GO1's shared-document cache is safe against every current caller of parse_model_document in gnd evolve: the loader, guards, validators and json_document only walk or build, and include composition clones the root before merging (model/_includes.py _merge), with GO1-C3 as the control for drift; R0.2 holds since all three loads keep their validations and the YAML guard keeps scanning. The phase graph is acyclic and the one-writer order is consistent. The seven concerns below are criterion-wording and lane gaps, none blocking: two criteria cannot pass a test written from their literal words (GO3-C3, GO2-C3's digest clause), one GO5-C2 fixture has no representable input, GO2 leaves the refused-candidate preview shape unstated, GO2's lane omits three existing preview consumers, and two consistency nits in the obligations and coordination claims.

criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, the software does not demonstrably do what it claims. Do not manufacture completeness concerns to avoid an empty return -- "no concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.
For this plan, a concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, a phase cannot be specified, implemented or tested as written, or the milestone would not do what its goal claims.

Can each phase GO1, GO2, GO3, GO4 and GO5 be specified, implemented and tested as section 2 and section 4 write it, within the scope sections 1 and 7 state? Is any criterion in section 4 impossible, unfalsifiable or dependent on one machine's speed?
